title: Local regular equations for a closed immersion of smooth schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion over $S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every $y\in Y$ there are an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $i(y)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], an integer $b\geq0$ and elements $f_1,\ldots,f_b\in A$ such that $Y\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}(A/(f_1,\ldots,f_b))$ as a closed subscheme of $U$ [def-pc-base-change], and $f_1,\ldots,f_b$ is an $A$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]: multiplication by $f_j$ on $A/(f_1,\ldots,f_{j-1})$ is injective for every $j$, and the final quotient is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 067U, lemma-immersion-smooth-into-smooth-regular-immersion, with regular immersion as in Tag 063J, definition-regular-immersion; the affine regular-equation consequence is used explicitly in more-morphisms.tex Tag 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure, first proof paragraph.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of the base image of $y$, then an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $i(y)$ contained in its inverse image. A closed immersion has affine inverse image $V=i^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}C$, and its section map $\varphi:A\to C$ is surjective [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The two structure maps on sections are compatible with $\varphi$ and smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. Let $Q$ be the prime corresponding to $i(y)$; naturality of the affine prime correspondence gives $\ker\varphi\subseteq Q$.

Apply [lem-pur-smooth-quotient-regular-sequence] to these smooth $R$-algebras and $\varphi$. It supplies $g\notin Q$. Replace $U$ by its affine basic open $D(g)$. Sections on that open form a model of $A[1/g]$, so the theorem gives a regular list $f$ generating the extended kernel. Restriction of the quasi-coherent kernel ideal equals the kernel of the new section map. Therefore this new kernel is exactly $(f)$.

The new open contains $i(y)$ because $g\notin Q$. Its inverse image under $i$ is affine, and its section map is surjective. The first isomorphism theorem identifies its section ring with $A/(f)$. Combine the affine spectrum isomorphism of the inverse image with this quotient isomorphism and the canonical pullback-restriction isomorphism. Naturality of the spectrum map gives the required equality with the pullback projection. These are exactly the isomorphism and commutative equation in the statement, with the regular list obtained in the preceding step.

proof_origin.place: Tag 067U, lemma-immersion-smooth-into-smooth-regular-immersion, affine reduction to Tag 067T and the separately stated flat-family criterion Tag 063W(2). Fibre regularity and the regular-local parameter argument are proved in the smooth-algebra corollary.

lean.statement: theorem exists_regular_equations_of_smooth_closedImmersion {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ S) (q : Y ⟶ S) (i : Y ⟶ X) [Smooth p] [Smooth q] [IsClosedImmersion i] (hi : i ≫ p = q) (y : Y) : ∃ U : X.Opens, i y ∈ U ∧ ∃ (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (a : U.toScheme ≅ Spec A) (f : List A), RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular A f ∧ ∃ e : pullback i U.ι ≅ Spec (CommRingCat.of (A ⧸ Ideal.ofList f)), e.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.ofList f))) = pullback.snd i U.ι ≫ a.hom
